info.title: Screeps standalone server socket API
info.description: Socket protocol of a standalone, single-world Screeps server (for example OpenScreeps) as the official web client uses it when `options.official` is false and as the official private server (screeps/backend-local) implements it. Composed from the official Screeps World socket contract and the standalone compatibility profile; each message's `x-profile` states whether it is unchanged (`required`) or has documented standalone differences (`adapted`). Channel names carry no shard. Session tokens are short-lived: every `auth ok` and every authenticated HTTP response can issue a replacement that must be stored.

standalone.description: SockJS endpoint `/socket` of the standalone server; the raw WebSocket transport is `/socket/websocket`. Use `wss` when the host terminates TLS.

host.description: Standalone server hostname or IP address.

excluded.package: The private-server socket greets with `time` and `protocol` only; `package` announces official desktop client releases.
excluded.serverDown: Maintenance notices are part of the hosted service; the private-server socket never sends `server down`.
excluded.cannotSubscribe: The private-server socket rejects subscriptions silently and never sends `cannot subscribe` lines.
excluded.userSteamPurchaseEvent: Steam purchases are a hosted account service; private servers do not publish `steam-purchase` events.

adaptations.authOk: Standalone tokens are session tokens: `auth ok` issues a new one with a short lifetime that replaces the stored token.
adaptations.roomEvent: One world: the room channel is `room:<room>` without a shard, and room events carry no `decorations`.
adaptations.roomErrorEvent: One world: the room error channel is `err@room:<room>` without a shard.
adaptations.roomMapEvent: One world: the map channel is `roomMap2:<room>` without a shard.
adaptations.mapVisualEvent: One world: the map visual channel is `mapVisual:<user>` without a shard.
adaptations.userMemoryEvent: One world: Memory watch channels are `user:<user>/memory/<path>` without a shard.
adaptations.userConsoleEvent: One world: console events carry no `shard`.
adaptations.userCodeEvent: backend-local sends the branch document's save time as stored: a date (an ISO 8601 string) for branches saved by `POST /api/user/clone-branch` (override: UserCode).

authOk.description: Unframed protocol line `auth ok <token>`, sent uncompressed. The token is a newly issued session token that expires after about a minute unless used; store it in place of the sent token for later `auth` commands and HTTP requests. The official client replaces its stored token with it, then sends the subscriptions it queued.

roomEvent.summary: Detailed, incremental updates of one room (`room:<room>`).
roomEvent.description: Requires authentication. The first event after subscribing is the full room; later events are diffs against what this connection already received (see `RoomObjectsDiff`), sent at most once per tick. Each user receives at most two room subscriptions per update across all connections; subscriptions beyond that receive `err@room:` events instead and resume when selected again. Rooms that do not exist are ignored silently.

roomMapEvent.summary: Low-detail positions of one room for the world map (`roomMap2:<room>`).

mapVisualEvent.summary: The subscribing user's map visuals of the previous tick (`mapVisual:<user>`).

userMemoryEvent.summary: The value at one Memory path (`user:<user>/memory/<path>`).

UserCode.x-profile-reason: backend-local re-reads the branch document for the event: `POST /api/user/code` stores milliseconds, `POST /api/user/clone-branch` a date, which arrives as an ISO 8601 string.

timestamp.description: Save time: milliseconds since the Unix epoch, or an ISO 8601 date-time for branches saved by `POST /api/user/clone-branch`.

UserConsole.x-profile-reason: One world: console events carry no `shard`.

RoomEvent.x-profile-reason: Room events of a standalone server carry no `decorations`.
RoomEvent.description: One room update. The first event after subscribing carries `users` (including the built-in users) and `info`, plus `flags` when the subscribing user has flags in the room; later events carry `objects`, `gameTime` and `visual`, `info` for world rooms (`W1N1`-style names), `flags` when the subscribing user has flags, and `users` when objects reference users not sent before. The official client shallow-merges `users` into the users it holds.
